title: Normalized relative restriction mate on injective models
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site in a universe containing all parameter sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules $\mathcal M_R$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and action categories $\mathcal A_P(R)$ for the condensed group $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $G,H$ be profinite groups, $u:\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to H$ a continuous homomorphism and $\tau=u(1)$. Write $L_J^G$ for trivial-$J$ inflation and $\Gamma_J^G$ for its invariant-inclusion-normalized right adjoint, retaining $G$, for $J=H,\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$. Let $V=\operatorname{Res}_{1_G\times u}$, $U_J:\mathcal A_{G\times J}(R)\to\mathcal A_J(R)$ and $U_0:\mathcal A_G(R)\to\mathcal M_R$ forget $G$. Write $Q$ for ordinary derived localization and $\alpha^G_{J,P}:Q\Gamma_J^G P\to R\Gamma_J^G(QP)$ for its canonical computation unit on bounded-below complexes. Using the normalized adjunctions $D(L_J^G)\dashv R\Gamma_J^G$, the identity $V L_H^G=L_{\mathbf Z}^G$ has a canonical derived mate
$$\beta^G:R\Gamma_H^G\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G D(V).$$
For every bounded-below complex $P$ it satisfies the actual derived-arrow equation
$$\beta^G_{QP}\alpha^G_{H,P}=\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,VP}Q(\iota_P),$$
where $\iota_P:\Gamma_H^G P\to\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G VP$ is termwise invariant inclusion. Its $H^0$ on modules is that inclusion. The mate commutes with canonical shifts and triangle boundaries.

The equality of fixed-section submodules $U_0\Gamma_J^G=\Gamma_{R,J}U_J$ induces natural isomorphisms
$$\delta_J:D(U_0)R\Gamma_J^G\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{R,J}D(U_J)$$
fixed on every bounded-below injective complex by the identical invariant inclusions and computation units. Under the literal commutation of $U$ with $V$, these isomorphisms take $D(U_0)(\beta^G)$ to the canonical scalar derived restriction of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], as an equality of natural transformations, not only on cohomology. The $\delta_J$ commute with canonical shifts and boundaries. Restriction of an injective need not be injective; the displayed mate equation holds without that hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting] to $J=H,\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}$. It gives Grothendieck relative action categories, exact normalized inflation adjunctions, enough injectives and exact injective-preserving $U_J,U_0$. The map $1_G\times u:G\times\mathbf Z_{\mathrm{disc}}\to G\times H$ is a continuous group homomorphism, coordinatewise. Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] to these groups and this homomorphism: $V$ is exact, and $\mathcal M_R,\mathcal A_J(R)$ are Grothendieck with exact normalized adjunctions $T_J\dashv\Gamma_{R,J}$. Thus [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction] supplies both relative and scalar derived adjunctions and their computation-unit/counit identities. All these Grothendieck categories admit K-injective resolutions [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective], so the unbounded right derived functors $(R\Gamma^u,\alpha^u)$ exist and $\alpha^u$ is invertible on K-injectives [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], in particular on bounded-below injective complexes [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. By (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] there is a unique $\gamma:R\Gamma\to R\Gamma^u|_{D^+}$ with $\gamma_{QP}\alpha_P=\alpha^u_P$; at a bounded-below injective $I$ both units are invertible by (2), so $\gamma_{QI}$ is, and every bounded-below $P$ has such a resolution [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence]; so $\gamma$ is an isomorphism. The unbounded counit satisfies the underived-counit identity of [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived]; comparing with the counit identity above at $QI$ and using naturality, it agrees with the bounded-below counit under $D(L)(\gamma)$. So under $\gamma$ the two adjunctions, computation units and $H^0$ identifications agree. Use these normalized adjunctions throughout, in the fixed coefficient universe.

proof.text: The identity $V L_H^G=L_{\mathbf Z}^G$ holds on objects and maps because restriction of a trivial action is trivial. Its underived mate is the transpose of the restricted counit $L_{\mathbf Z}^G\Gamma_H^G M\to VM$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. That counit is inclusion of $H$-fixed sections. An $H$-fixed section after every base change is fixed by each $u(z)$, and this inclusion respects residual $G$ since the two actions commute. By the normalized transpose formula of [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting], its transpose is precisely $\iota_M$, with no automorphism of the invariant object inserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-mate-model] with $L=L_H^G$, $L'=L_{\mathbf Z}^G$, its horizontal functor on retained-action categories equal to the identity, its other horizontal functor equal to $V$, and $\sigma$ the identity of step 2. The exactness and enough-injectives hypotheses are step 1. Since its underived mate is $\iota$, the conclusion is exactly $\beta^G_{QP}\alpha^G_{H,P}=\alpha^G_{\mathbf Z,VP}Q(\iota_P)$ for every bounded-below $P$. In particular this proves an equality of arrows, including when $VP$ is not injective. Apply [lem-kun-right-derived-single-h0] to this equation for $P=M[0]$ separately for the left exact right adjoints $\Gamma_H^G$ at $M$ and $\Gamma_{\mathbf Z}^G$ at $VM$, using the canonical termwise identification $D(V)(M[0])=(VM)[0]$. The canonical zeroth-homology identifications then give precisely $\iota_M$.

proof.text:
For each $J$ let $T_J:\mathcal M_R\to\mathcal A_J(R)$ be the exact scalar trivial inflation with normalized right adjoint supplied by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] for the topological group $J$. Its forward transpose restricts the codomain to the stated invariant subsheaf. Forgetting gives $U_J L_J^G=T_J U_0$ and $U_0\Gamma_J^G=\Gamma_{R,J}U_J$: both invariant submodules impose exactly the same fixed-section condition after every base change. Their counits are the identical inclusions. Take the derived mate $\delta_J$ of the first identity. Apply [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-mate-model] with $L=L_J^G$, $L'=T_J$, horizontal functors $U_0,U_J$; its underived mate is the second identity by the same normalized transpose formula. Consequently
$$\delta_{J,QP}D(U_0)(\alpha^G_{J,P})=\alpha_{R,J,U_JP}.$$
For every bounded-below injective complex $I$, both units on the two sides are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], since $U_J I$ is termwise injective by [lem-sfb-product-action-exact-forgetting]. Thus $\delta_{J,QI}=\alpha_{R,J,U_JI}\,D(U_0)(\alpha^G_{J,I})^{-1}$ is invertible and is the required identical-invariants comparison. Every bounded-below $P$ has an injective resolution by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence]; naturality along its invertible localized augmentation proves invertibility of $\delta_J$ everywhere and uniqueness with this normalization.

proof.text:
Write $b_u$ for scalar restriction, normalized by [lem-sfb-condensed-restriction-mate-normalization] (and hence the restriction of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]). Compare
$$A=\delta_{\mathbf Z,D(V)(-)}\,D(U_0)(\beta^G),\qquad B=b_{u,D(U_H)(-)}\,\delta_H.$$
For a bounded-below injective $I$, precompose both with $D(U_0)(\alpha^G_{H,I})$. Steps 3 and 4 turn $A$ into $\alpha_{R,\mathbf Z,U_{\mathbf Z}VI}\,Q(U_0\iota_I)$. The scalar computation-unit equation turns $B$ into $\alpha_{R,\mathbf Z,u^*U_HI}\,Q(\iota_{U_HI})$. These are identical: $U_{\mathbf Z}V=u^*U_H$ literally, and both inclusions send a fixed section to itself. Cancel the invertible source unit; then transport along any injective resolution using naturality. This gives $A=B$ as natural transformations on $D^+$, without assuming $VI$ injective.

proof.text: The Grothendieck categories in step 1 admit K-injective resolutions by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. Apply [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift] to their exact inflation adjunctions (including scalar inflation). Their canonical derived units and counits commute with the fixed signed shifts. On bounded-below objects these are the normalized adjunctions of step 1, under its identification $\gamma$; the shift of $R\Gamma$ is the one transported along $\gamma$ from the K-injective shift. Exact $V,U_J,U_0$ have their termwise shift comparisons by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For $F_J=R\Gamma_J^G$, the mate formula is $\beta_X^G=F_{\mathbf Z}(D(V)\varepsilon_{H,X})\eta_{\mathbf Z,F_HX}$. Substitute the unit and counit shift identities in this formula: each factor on $X[n]$ becomes the corresponding shifted factor on $X$. This proves shift compatibility of $\beta^G$. The identical substitution in $\delta_{J,X}=R\Gamma_{R,J}(D(U_J)\varepsilon_{J,X})\eta_{R,J,D(U_0)F_JX}$ proves shift compatibility of $\delta_J$.

source.place: Tags 070J, 070K, 09T5; bounded-below injective models and fixed derived-adjunction shifts

proof.text: Right derived functors are triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], and exact derived $V,U_J,U_0$ are triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For any natural transformation $t:F\to F'$ just constructed and triangle boundary $d:C\to A[1]$, naturality gives $t_{A[1]}F(d)=F'(d)t_C$. Substitute step 6's shift equation for $t_{A[1]}$ to obtain $t_A[1]s_FF(d)=s_{F'}F'(d)t_C$, with $s_F,s_{F'}$ the canonical shift comparisons. This is exactly the last-arrow square of the image triangles. The other squares are ordinary naturality. It proves the asserted boundary compatibility for both $\beta^G$ and every $\delta_J$.
